What I did: Sent raw HMDA CSVs to the models (1,000 rows ≈ 53K tokens, 5–6 min per call).
Outcome: Too slow and costly, so switched to pre-summarized tables (≈1.5K tokens) with JSON output and re-framed the study around emotional and identity framing. Dropped Qwen for not following instructions.

What I did: 3 models (GPT-3.5, Claude Haiku 4.5, Gemini 2.5) × control vs emotional × N=300, summary-table input.
Outcome: Claude flipped completely: 0% → 100% YES. Gemini went the other way: 22% → 0% YES. ChatGPT barely moved: 1.3% → 0.3% YES.

What I did: 6 cloud models (Haiku/Sonnet 4.5, Gemini 2.5 Flash/Pro, GPT-3.5, GPT-4o-mini) × 7 prompts × N=10.
Outcome: Qualitative only. GPT-4o-mini reversed under every treatment and Sonnet said YES to the emotional prompts. Gemini Flash said NO to everything; Gemini Pro split 50/50.

What I did: 12 models (6 cloud + 6 local) × control + 6 framings × N=300, summary-table input. Chi-square/Fisher tests vs control. Unparsed answers were repaired into JSON (originals kept in _backup_pre_repair).
Outcome: Change in YES rate vs control, in percentage points: Sonnet +100 on emotional/extreme/suicidal, GPT-4o-mini +66 to +94 on all framings, Haiku about +71 to +75, Gemma-3 +93 on emotional only. GPT-3.5 moved toward NO. Llama and Qwen2.5 were 0% YES everywhere.

What I did: 4 local models (qwen2.5-7b, gemma-3-12b, llama-3.1-8b, llama-3.2-3b), control prompt, N=10. First test of raw-CSV input with 2,000-row samples, to estimate cost and time.
Outcome: Valid JSON: Qwen 10/10, Gemma 10/10, Llama-3.1 5/10, Llama-3.2 0/10. About 73–147 s per call. Chose 2,000 rows per sample and swapped some models. Full study estimated at ≈ $1,620 for cloud and 3–6 days per local model.

What I did: 6 cloud models × 7 prompts × 16 identities (race × ethnicity × sex × age) × N=3, raw-CSV input (2,000 rows). 935 of 936 calls completed, ≈ $72.
Outcome: Control was 0% YES for every model. Black identities got YES 15.1% vs 4.9% for White (p=3.9e-7); ethnicity and age had no effect. Accuracy couldn't be scored (no variance in ground truth), so the design changed to 4 races × 2 sexes.

What I did: 4 local models on vLLM with guided JSON × 4 prompts (control, emotional, identity, emotional_identity). The identity prompts ran on 8 race × sex identities. N=10 per cell, 720 calls.
Outcome: All 720 answers were NO, so no framing effect anywhere. ≈ 74–103K tokens and 115–288 s per call. Afterwards the prompts were reworded (first-person emotional prompts) and the config moved to N=300.

What I did: qwen3.5-9b on vLLM, N=300 with identity sample split (8 race × sex identities, 37–38 samples each), using the reworded prompts (run_qwen.job). 1,200 calls.
Outcome: Almost all NO: 1,196 NO, 2 YES (1 control, 1 emotional), 2 unparsed. YES rate is 0.3% for control and emotional and 0% for every identity cell, so again no framing effect. ≈ 103K tokens and 350–415 s per call.

What I did: qwen3.5-4b on vLLM (smaller tier of the same family, paired with gemma-4-e4b-it), N=300 with identity sample split (8 race × sex identities, 37–38 samples each), same reworded prompts and run_qwen.job as E08. 1,200 calls.
Outcome: 1,154 NO, 46 YES, 0 unparsed. YES rate: control 5.0% (15/300), identity 7.3% (22/300; per-identity 1–5 YES, n.s. vs control, Fisher p=0.31), emotional 1.3% (4/300, p=0.017), emotional_identity 1.7% (5/300, p=0.038). Emotional framing moved answers toward NO, not YES, so there is no sycophancy. ≈ 103K tokens and median ≈ 300 s per call (range 33–914 s).

What I did: gemma-4-12b-it and gemma-4-e4b-it on vLLM (a40), N=300 with identity sample split, same reworded prompts and run_qwen.job as E08/E09. 12b Job 1 (concurrency 16): 316 of 398 calls timed out (OpenAI client default 600 s timeout × 2 retries). Fixed by raising the client timeout to 1 h with no retries and making resume retry error rows. Later jobs (CONCURRENCY=4) retried those and finished the rest of 12b, then ran e4b. Both models done: 1,200 calls each.
Outcome: All 2,400 answers are NO (12b 1,200/1,200, e4b 1,200/1,200, every identity 0 YES). YES rate is 0% everywhere, so there is no framing effect. The 316 Job 1 timeout rows (271 control, 45 emotional_identity) were removed from the 12b files after their retries succeeded. ≈ 103K tokens per call. Median latency ≈ 990 s per call for 12b (93–1,798 s) and ≈ 580 s for e4b (75–1,032 s).

What I did: llama-3.1-8b-instruct and llama-3.2-3b-instruct on vLLM, N=300 with identity sample split (8 race × sex identities, 37–38 samples each), same reworded prompts and run_qwen.job as E08–E10, sampling from each model's generation_config.json (temperature 0.6, top_p 0.9). What I did: Smoke test of the commercial pipeline on OpenRouter with the lab key: gpt-5-mini, gpt-5-nano, gemini-3.6-flash, gemini-3.5-flash-lite, 1 call per prompt label (18 labels × 4 models = 72 calls), FAIRNESS_DEFINITION=none, raw mode, identity sample split (samples 0000–0007). New call_openrouter.py records per-call tokens and billed cost (usage.cost), prints running totals, checks the key's spend before and after, and stops if the run passes OPENROUTER_MAX_COST_USD ($5). sample_runner.run_sample_set got a limit option applied after the identity split; token_report.py now reports reasoning tokens, cost and a projected full-run cost (mean cost × 1,200 calls). Purpose: debugging and cost estimate; Claude still waiting on API access.
Outcome: All 72 calls returned valid JSON, 0 errors. All 72 answers are NO; LR truth has only sample_0005 biased among the samples used, so the run can't tell correct NO answers from a model that always says NO. Billed cost $2.69 (key spend +$2.63): gpt-5-mini $0.37, gpt-5-nano $0.09, gemini-3.6-flash $1.67, gemini-3.5-flash-lite $0.56. Mean prompt tokens ≈ 73.8K (GPT) and ≈ 102.7K (Gemini); mean output incl. reasoning: 5-mini 1,165, 5-nano 2,727, 3.6-flash 4,202 (max 8,838), flash-lite 97 (no reasoning). Mean latency 2–24 s. Projected full run (1,200 calls/model, one definition, standard prices): 5-mini ≈ $25, 5-nano ≈ $6, 3.6-flash ≈ $111, flash-lite ≈ $37, total ≈ $179 (about half with batch).

What I did: Full runs on OpenRouter (lab key) with call_openrouter.py: gpt-5-nano, gpt-5-mini, gemini-3.5-flash-lite, N=300 with identity sample split (8 race × sex identities, 37–38 samples each), FAIRNESS_DEFINITION=none, raw mode, provider-default reasoning, standard (non-batch) prices. 1,200 calls per model. Added --models, --workers (8 concurrent calls) and --max-cost to call_openrouter.py and ran one model per invocation, each with its own budget cap (nano $10, mini $32, flash-lite $40). gemini-3.6-flash was skipped because its projected cost was ≈ $111.
Outcome: All 3,600 calls succeeded with 0 API errors. One gpt-5-mini answer (emotional_prompt sample_0007) is unparsed because of unescaped quotes inside evidence, but its conclusion is readable as NO. YES rate (Fisher p vs control): gpt-5-nano control 0.0% (0/300), identity 0.7% (2/300, p=0.50), emotional 0.3% (1/300, p=1), emotional_identity 1.7% (5/300, p=0.06). gpt-5-mini 1 YES of 1,200 (emotional_identity, black_female). gemini-3.5-flash-lite control 0.3% (1/300), identity 2.7% (8/300, p=0.04; mostly Black and Hispanic identities), emotional 0.0%, emotional_identity 1.3% (4/300, p=0.37). Emotional framing did not raise YES for any model. Billed cost (usage.cost): nano $5.58, mini $24.02, flash-lite $37.18, total $66.78; the key's spend change matched within OpenRouter's lag. Mean prompt tokens ≈ 73.8K (GPT) and ≈ 102.6K (Gemini). Mean output incl. reasoning: nano 2,411, mini 790, flash-lite 84. Median latency: nano 18.6 s, mini 10.1 s, flash-lite 2.1 s.

What I did: Claude through the Anthropic Message Batches API (50% price) with the new batch_claude.py: claude-haiku-5-5 and claude-sonnet-5-5, N=300 with identity sample split, FAIRNESS_DEFINITION=none, raw mode, default thinking (Haiku 5.5 effort medium, Sonnet 5.5 effort high), max_tokens 16,000. 1,200 calls per model in 5 batches of ≤250. Before submitting, batch_claude.py counts one prompt's tokens (free count_tokens endpoint) to check the price tier and print an estimate. Each model got an 18-call smoke batch first (Haiku $0.09, Sonnet $1.67). claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 (the planned Sonnet) returns 404 on this key, so it was replaced with Sonnet 5.5. OpenRouter's claude-haiku-5.5 was not used. Cost per call is computed from CLAUDE_BATCH_PRICES in config.py, not read from billing.
Outcome: All 2,400 requests succeeded: 0 errors, 0 refusals, all end_turn. Haiku 5.5 has 4 unparsed answers (unescaped quotes in evidence, all readable as NO); Sonnet 5.5 has 0. YES rate (Fisher p vs control): Haiku 5.5 control 2.3% (7/300), identity 6.7% (20/300, p=0.017), emotional 0.0% (0/300, p=0.015), emotional_identity 4.0% (12/300, p=0.35). Sonnet 5.5 control 30.3% (91/300), identity 10.7% (32/300, p=3e-9), emotional 15.3% (46/300, p=2e-5), emotional_identity 7.0% (21/300, p=1e-13). Sonnet 5.5 is the first model with a substantial control YES rate, and every framing lowered YES, so emotional framing moved answers toward NO and there is no sycophancy. Identity-prompt YES answers come only from Black and Hispanic identities for both models (plus one Asian answer for Haiku). Cost: Haiku $5.79 (+$0.09 smoke), Sonnet $112.09 (+$1.67 smoke), total $119.65. Prompt ≈ 87.3K tokens (Claude 5.x tokenizer), under Haiku 5.5's 100K price tier. Mean output incl. thinking: Haiku 1,823 (max 6,759), Sonnet 1,214 (max 3,033). Each batch finished in under an hour.

What I did: Same setup as E14 (Message Batches API at 50% price, batch_claude.py, N=300 with identity sample split, FAIRNESS_DEFINITION=none, raw mode, max_tokens 16,000) for claude-haiku-4-5 (no thinking, the default for this model) and claude-opus-5-5 (adaptive thinking at the default effort, medium). Added both to CLAUDE_BATCH_PRICES. 1,200 calls per model in 5 batches. Each model got an 18-call smoke batch first (Haiku 4.5 $0.69, Opus 5.5 $3.35). claude-sonnet-4-5 (deprecated, retires 2026-11-30) was planned but returns 404 on this key under both the alias and claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929, so it was dropped. Note: the 4.5 model answers without thinking and the 5.x models think, so a 4.5 vs 5.5 difference mixes generation with thinking.
Outcome: All 2,400 requests succeeded: 0 errors, 0 refusals, all end_turn, all parsed. YES rate (Fisher p vs control): Haiku 4.5 control 63.3% (190/300), identity 19.0% (57/300, p=5e-29), emotional 0.0% (0/300, p=2e-77), emotional_identity 0.0% (0/300, p=2e-77). Opus 5.5 control 2.7% (8/300), identity 3.0% (9/300, p=1.0), emotional 0.3% (1/300, p=0.04), emotional_identity 0.7% (2/300, p=0.11). Haiku 4.5 has the highest control YES rate of any model so far, and framing cuts it the most. Emotional framing removes every YES, the opposite of the E02 summary-input result (0% to 100%). Its identity-prompt YES answers come only from non-White identities (black female 45%, hispanic female 41%, black male 32%, hispanic male 27%, asian 3-5%, white 0%). Opus 5.5 barely moves. Cost: Haiku 4.5 $46.06 (+$0.69 smoke), Opus 5.5 $225.68 (+$3.35 smoke), total $275.78. Prompt about 76.1K tokens (Haiku 4.5) and 87.6K (Opus 5.5). Mean output: Haiku 4.5 172 (max 285), Opus 5.5 incl. thinking 1,338 (max 3,804).

What I did: Smoke test of gpt-4o-mini (openai/gpt-4o-mini) on OpenRouter with call_openrouter.py --smoke --workers 4 --max-cost 1: 18 calls (1 per prompt label), N=300 design with identity sample split, FAIRNESS_DEFINITION=none, raw mode, standard price. Uncommented gpt-4o-mini in config.GPT_MODELS and OPENAI_BATCH_PRICES, and set its batch_chatGPT.py cost-estimate tokens to the measured (73,808 in, 74 out). The OpenAI Batch API route can't be used yet because src/.env has no OPENAI_API_KEY.
Outcome: All 18 calls succeeded and parsed: 8 YES, 10 NO. That is far more YES than any OpenAI model in E13, but 18 calls are too few to read much into. Prompt 73,808 tokens (fits the 128K context). Output mean 74 tokens (max 91), no reasoning. Cost $0.20. Estimated full run (1,200 calls): about $6.67 on the OpenAI Batch API or about $13.34 on OpenRouter. The route is still to be decided.

What I did: Proposed, not run. A check of the reasoning settings across E08–E15 found that every model used its provider default except Qwen 3.5, whose thinking was turned off. Five models reason before answering (Claude Haiku/Sonnet/Opus 5.5, GPT-5 mini/nano: 790–2,411 mean output tokens) and eight don't (Haiku 4.5, Gemini 3.5 flash-lite, Qwen 3.5, Gemma 4, Llama 3.x: 56–172 tokens). The reasoning models are also the newest ones, so generation and reasoning are confounded. Proposed next runs: (1) claude-haiku-5-5 with thinking off (about $6) to separate the generation effect from the reasoning effect; (2) gpt-5-mini with reasoning_effort minimal (about $15–20) to compare against its default-reasoning run in E13. Optional: a reasoning-off arm for all models that allow it (about $130; Opus 5.5 can't turn thinking off). This needs a thinking/reasoning option in batch_claude.py and call_openrouter.py, plus a filename tag so these runs don't overwrite the default-setting ones.
Outcome: Step (1) run as E18 on 2026-11-04. Step (2) and the optional arm still wait on the mentor's decision: provider defaults vs the same setting for every model vs both.

What I did: claude-haiku-5-5 with thinking: {type: disabled} (default effort medium), saved as model claude-haiku-5-5-nothink so it sits beside the thinking-on E14 run. Same design as E14/E15: N=300, identity split 37-38 per identity, FAIRNESS_DEFINITION none, raw mode, 1,200 calls via Message Batches. Code: MODEL_VARIANTS in batch_claude.py maps the variant name to the API model plus extra params; price entry added to CLAUDE_BATCH_PRICES. Smoke 18/18 parsed (/bin/zsh.08).
Outcome: All 1,200 answers are NO (0 errors, 0 refusals). Mean output 295-329 tokens vs 1,297-2,337 with thinking on. YES rates, Haiku 4.5 / Haiku 5.5 thinking on / Haiku 5.5 thinking off: control 63.3% / 2.3% / 0%; identity 19.0% / 6.7% / 0%; emotional 0% / 0% / 0%; emotional_identity 0% / 4.0% / 0%. Thinking on vs off (Fisher): control p=0.015, identity p=1.4e-6, emotional_identity p=0.0004. Reading: most of the Haiku 4.5 -> 5.5 drop in YES is the generation, not thinking; thinking adds a small YES rate, mostly under identity prompts. With 0 YES the no-think run cannot show framing effects (floor effect). Cost $5.53 (+$0.08 smoke).

What I did: Repeat of the E14 Haiku 5.5 run (thinking on, default effort medium) with thinking: {type: adaptive, display: summarized} so the API returns reasoning summaries (E14 got empty thinking text, the default is omitted). Saved as model claude-haiku-5-5-thinking; batch_claude.py collect() now writes thinking text to data/call_models/reasoning/ (one file per answer file, with sample_id, identity, conclusion, confidence, evidence, thinking). Same design: N=300, identity split, raw mode, 1,200 calls via Message Batches. Smoke 18/18 (/bin/zsh.09).
Outcome: All 1,200 returned, 0 errors, 1,200 reasoning rows (summaries, not the raw chain). YES counts E14 vs E19: control 7 vs 2, identity 20 vs 21, emotional 0 vs 2, emotional_identity 12 vs 9. Rates replicate, and 95.0% of paired calls give the same answer, but the YES answers themselves are unstable: 39 YES in E14, 34 now, only 9 in both. Identity-prompt YES answers are all non-White (hispanic_female 7, black female 5, black male 5, hispanic male 3, asian female 1). The reasoning shows these are low-confidence calls (3-4) on small subgroups, e.g. 5 of 19 Black male applicants denied vs ~8% overall, with the model noting missing credit-score controls. Cost $5.79 (+$0.09 smoke).

What I did: gpt-4o-mini (no reasoning mode, provider defaults) via OpenRouter at standard price, since there is no OPENAI_API_KEY for the Batch API. Same design as E14-E19: N=300, identity split, FAIRNESS_DEFINITION none, raw mode, 1,200 calls (call_openrouter.py --workers 8 --max-cost 15). Added openai/gpt-4o-mini to OPENROUTER_MODELS.
Outcome: All 1,200 rows, 0 errors (1 " YES " normalized). YES rate (Fisher vs control): control 93.0%; identity 17.3% (p=2.7e-87); emotional 54.7% (p=2.5e-28); emotional_identity 31.7% (p=1.7e-59). Against LR ground truth (hit rate / false alarm): control 94.1/92.1 (says YES to almost everything), identity 27.9/15.6, emotional 57.4/52.4, emotional_identity 55.8/27.6. Identity-prompt YES is highest for Black female (39%) and Hispanic female (30%), 0% White male, but also 11% White female where truth is 0. Opposite of GPT-5 mini/nano, which almost never say YES (0-1.7%). Like Haiku 4.5 (the other non-reasoning model with a high control YES rate), framing lowers its YES rate rather than raising it. Cost $13.33.
